senses.definition: Water that has frozen into a solid.
senses.example: The ice on the puddle cracked under my boot.

senses.definition: To cover a cake or other baked food with a sweet coating.
senses.example: We iced the cookies after they cooled.

senses.definition: A sweet mixture spread or drawn on cakes and other baked foods.
senses.example: We used blue icing to make waves on the cake.

senses.definition: Putting a sweet coating on a cake or other baked food. This is the -ing form of “ice.”
senses.example: We were icing the cupcakes when our cousins arrived.

senses.definition: Covered with ice or very cold.
senses.example: The icy steps were slippery before the sun warmed them.

senses.definition: A thought, plan, or suggestion.
senses.example: Rina had an idea for keeping the poster from curling.

senses.definition: One of two babies who began from the same fertilized egg and usually have very similar DNA.
senses.example: An identical twin can have likes and interests that differ from the other twin’s.

senses.definition: To find out and say who someone is or what something is.
senses.example: We used the field guide to identify the yellow flower.

senses.definition: A group of words that means something different as a group from what the separate words might suggest.
senses.example: In the idiom “piece of cake,” the speaker means a task was easy.

senses.definition: Doing no work or taking part in no activity.
senses.example: The swing stayed idle until the children came outside.

senses.definition: To keep running without moving or doing useful work, as an engine can.
senses.example: The school bus idled briefly before moving away.

senses.definition: Rock made when melted material cools and becomes solid.
senses.example: Obsidian is an igneous rock that can have a glassy surface.

senses.definition: To choose not to notice someone or pay attention to something.
senses.example: I tried to ignore the tapping sound and finish my reading.

senses.definition: Sick or not feeling well.
senses.example: Mina stayed home because she felt ill.

senses.definition: Against the law.
senses.example: It is illegal to take someone else’s bike without permission.

senses.definition: A drawing or picture that shows something from a story or helps explain a subject.
senses.example: The illustration showed what Peter Rabbit saw in the garden.

senses.definition: The amount of picture detail a grid can store, often described by how many pixels it has across and down.
senses.example: The image resolution is 300 pixels across and 200 pixels tall.

senses.definition: Existing only in your thoughts or in a made-up story.
senses.example: The book describes an imaginary city under the ocean.

senses.definition: To form an idea or picture in your mind, even if it is not real or happening now.
senses.example: Imagine a playground floating in the clouds.

senses.definition: To copy someone’s actions, speech, or sound.
senses.example: I tried to imitate the bird’s whistle.

senses.definition: Happening right away or very near in time or place.
senses.example: We got an immediate answer when we asked for directions.

senses.definition: A person who comes to live in another country.
senses.example: The museum keeps records of immigrants who sailed into New York Harbor.

senses.definition: Worth paying special attention to because it matters or can make a difference.
senses.example: It is important to write your name on your schoolwork.

senses.definition: An idea or feeling you get about someone or something.
senses.example: My first impression was that the puzzle would be difficult.

senses.definition: A mark left by pressing something into a softer surface.
senses.example: The shell left an impression in the wet clay.

senses.definition: A copy of the way a person sounds or acts.
senses.example: Lee did a funny impression of the cartoon character.

senses.definition: In usual school examples with positive parts, a fraction whose top number is at least as large as its bottom number.
senses.example: Seven thirds is an improper fraction that means two wholes and one third.

senses.definition: To make something better or become better at it.
senses.example: Playing each day helped me improve at skipping rope.

senses.definition: Making up part of a performance as you do it.
senses.example: The trumpet player used improvisation to change the end of the tune.

senses.definition: In just a few words that cover the main idea.
senses.example: In a nutshell, the class voted to plant herbs instead of flowers.

senses.definition: Shared by two or more people or things.
senses.example: The puzzles have something in common. Both hide a triangle.

senses.definition: Over a long time, after the early results have passed.
senses.example: Mending the bag may take a little time, but in the long run it could save us money.

senses.definition: Something you pay for from inside a game or other app.
senses.example: We check with an adult before making an in-app purchase.

senses.definition: A unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot.
senses.example: The seedling grew about one inch in a week.

senses.definition: To move a little bit at a time.
senses.example: The kitten inched closer to the noisy toy.

senses.definition: Something that happened, especially an unusual event or problem.
senses.example: The teacher wrote a note about the incident with the dropped paint tray.

senses.definition: A front tooth with a sharp edge used for cutting into food.
senses.example: An incisor cut off a small piece of apple.

senses.definition: To have someone or something as part of a larger thing.
senses.example: Please include your younger brother in the game.

senses.definition: Money someone receives, often from work or a business.
senses.example: Sam earned some income by watering a neighbor’s garden each week.

senses.definition: To become larger or make something larger in amount, size, or number.
senses.example: Add more water to increase the amount of soup.

senses.definition: An amount by which something grows.
senses.example: The warmer days brought an increase in visitors to the park.

senses.definition: Very hard to believe because it seems so unusual or impressive.
senses.example: We saw an incredible rainbow above the waterfall.

senses.definition: Really or certainly, used to agree or stress that something is true.
senses.example: The climb was indeed steep near the top.

senses.definition: Able to act or do things without relying on someone or something else.
senses.example: Our kitten became more independent as it got older.

senses.definition: An organized set of clues that helps someone or something find information quickly.
senses.example: The search engine checked an index for pages about boats.

senses.definition: In chemistry, a substance that shows something about a liquid, often by changing color.
senses.example: A pH indicator can change from purple to pink in an acidic drink.

senses.definition: Going by a route or method that is not the straightest or simplest one.
senses.example: We took an indirect path so we could visit the lake first.

senses.definition: Being understood without being said plainly.
senses.example: The note gave an indirect clue by describing where birds drink.

senses.definition: A single person or thing, viewed separately from the group.
senses.example: Each individual chose a book to read.

senses.definition: Meant for one person or thing at a time.
senses.example: We used individual bowls for the berries.

senses.definition: Inside a building.
senses.example: We took the game indoors when it thundered.

senses.definition: A kind of work or business that makes goods or provides services.
senses.example: Many people in our town work in the fishing industry.

senses.definition: Costing less than many things of the same kind.
senses.example: We chose an inexpensive notebook for our sketches.

senses.definition: The power to change how someone thinks or acts or how something happens.
senses.example: My cousin’s interest in birds had an influence on what I chose to study.

senses.definition: To affect what someone thinks or how something happens.
senses.example: Weather can influence which games we play at recess.

senses.definition: To tell someone facts or useful details.
senses.example: Please inform the office if you leave school early.

senses.definition: Facts or details that help you learn about someone or something.
senses.example: The map gives information about where each trail starts.

senses.definition: A kind of light that human eyes cannot see. Warm things often give off infrared light.
senses.example: Webb can collect infrared light from a cloud of dust.

senses.definition: One of the foods or other things mixed together to make something.
senses.example: A spoonful of cocoa is the last ingredient in our drink.

senses.definition: To get a feature or piece of genetic information from biological parents.
senses.example: Children inherit different mixes of DNA.

senses.definition: Happening at the first stage of something.
senses.example: Our initial plan was to make a round kite.

senses.definition: The first letter of a name or word, often used in place of the whole name.
senses.example: I put my initials at the bottom of the drawing.

senses.definition: To hurt a person’s or animal’s body.
senses.example: The squirrel fell from the fence but did not injure its paw.

senses.definition: Harm or damage to a body part.
senses.example: The minor injury kept me out of soccer for the rest of the afternoon.

senses.definition: A colored substance used to write, draw, or print.
senses.example: The pen ran out of ink halfway through my note.

senses.definition: To add ink or go over a drawing in ink.
senses.example: Yuki inked the pencil sketch after choosing the lines she wanted to keep.

senses.definition: A small place where travelers can pay to sleep and sometimes eat.
senses.example: We stayed in an inn beside the river.

senses.definition: Farther inside or closer to the middle.
senses.example: Close the inner door before opening the one that leads outside.

senses.definition: The part of the ear farthest from the outside that contains organs for hearing and balance.
senses.example: The inner ear sends clues about head movement to the brain.

senses.definition: One part of a baseball game in which each team has a turn to bat.
senses.example: Both teams scored in the third inning.

senses.definition: Not responsible for something wrong that happened.
senses.example: The other cat was innocent of spilling the food.

senses.definition: Unaware of danger or bad things.
senses.example: The puppy gave an innocent look before tugging the ribbon.

senses.definition: A number, fact, or signal you give to a rule, device, or system.
senses.example: In a number machine that adds two, an input of three gives five.

senses.definition: To ask for information.
senses.example: We called to inquire about the opening time for the pool.

senses.definition: Words or signs written, stamped, or cut onto a surface, such as stone, metal, or paper.
senses.example: The inscription on the statue’s base told us who it showed.

senses.definition: An animal whose adult form usually has six legs and three main body parts. Some insects have wings.
senses.example: A beetle is an insect, but a spider has eight legs.

senses.definition: To put something into a space or place in something else.
senses.example: Insert the card into the slot with its picture facing up.

senses.definition: A piece of paper or another part added inside something.
senses.example: The brochure had an insert with opening hours.

senses.definition: The part within something.
senses.example: The inside of the box was lined with soft cloth.

senses.definition: In or into a place within walls, edges, or a covering.
senses.example: We carried the chairs inside.

senses.definition: Within the space or limits of something.
senses.example: An old note was tucked inside the envelope.

senses.definition: To say very firmly that something is true or must happen.
senses.example: I insisted that we check the gate after the dog slipped out.

senses.definition: To examine something closely, often to check its condition.
senses.example: We inspected the wagon’s wheels before putting books in it.

senses.definition: To put something in place so it is ready to use.
senses.example: The school installed a new clock in the hallway.

senses.definition: To put a program on a device so you can run it.
senses.example: I asked Dad to help install the drawing app.

senses.definition: A very short amount of time or one point in time.
senses.example: For an instant I thought the box was moving on its own.

senses.definition: Happening right away or ready after very little preparation.
senses.example: We got an instant reply from the library.

senses.definition: In place of someone or something else.
senses.example: We wanted oranges but bought apples instead.

senses.definition: To tell someone how to do something or what they should do.
senses.example: The coach instructed us to start behind the white line.

senses.definition: A direction that tells someone what to do or how to do it.
senses.example: The first instruction says to fold the paper in half.

senses.definition: A tool made for a particular kind of work or measurement.
senses.example: A compass is an instrument that helps us find north.

senses.definition: An object made to play music.
senses.example: Milo chose a brass instrument for the school band.

senses.definition: A feeling of wanting to learn more about something.
senses.example: The field trip sparked my interest in local birds.

senses.definition: Extra money paid for borrowing money or received for keeping money in certain accounts.
senses.example: The bank paid a little interest on my savings.

senses.definition: To make someone want to know more.
senses.example: The old map interested me because it showed a town that no longer exists.

senses.definition: A way one library borrows a book or other item from another library so a reader can use it.
senses.example: The librarian arranged an interlibrary loan for a book about local birds.

senses.definition: The worldwide system that connects many networks and lets computers exchange information.
senses.example: I can use the internet to send a message to someone far away.

senses.definition: To work out or explain what something means.
senses.example: We interpreted the red arrow as a sign to stop and turn around.

senses.definition: To say or sign what someone is saying in another language.
senses.example: A volunteer interpreted for visitors who did not speak English.

senses.definition: To stop something briefly by getting in its way or speaking before someone finishes.
senses.example: I did not mean to interrupt your story before the ending.

senses.definition: The part of the shore covered by water at high tide and exposed at low tide.
senses.example: The highest barnacles in the intertidal zone spend hours in the open air.

senses.definition: A long, folded tube in the body that helps take useful parts from food and carry along the rest.
senses.example: Your small intestine takes in most nutrients.

senses.definition: To create something new, such as a tool, game, or way of doing something.
senses.example: We invented a game that uses only three stones and a chalk circle.

senses.definition: A person who creates a new device or way of doing something.
senses.example: The inventor built three models before the machine worked.

senses.definition: Unable to be seen.
senses.example: The clear fishing line looked nearly invisible against the glass.

senses.definition: To ask someone to come somewhere or join in something.
senses.example: We invited the new student to sit with us.

senses.definition: To include someone or something as part of an activity, plan, or problem.
senses.example: The game involves every person in the class.

senses.definition: The colored ring in an eye that changes the size of the opening in its center.
senses.example: Her iris is brown.

senses.definition: An element that can be a metal and is also needed in tiny forms by the body to help carry oxygen.
senses.example: The beans in my lunch provide some iron.

senses.definition: Not following the usual rule or pattern.
senses.example: The past form “went” is an irregular form of “go.”

senses.definition: Uneven in shape or spacing.
senses.example: We made a path with irregular pieces of stone.

senses.definition: Bringing water to land or plants with pipes, channels, or other equipment, especially when rain alone is not enough.
senses.example: The farm uses drip irrigation to send water to the roots of the plants.

senses.definition: An area of land with water all around it.
senses.example: We watched birds land on a small island in the lake.

senses.definition: A problem or subject that people are discussing.
senses.example: Getting enough chairs was the only issue with the plan.

senses.definition: One edition of a magazine or similar publication.
senses.example: The next issue of the magazine has a puzzle page.

senses.definition: To officially give out or announce something.
senses.example: The library issues a new card when you sign up.

senses.definition: A narrow strip of land that joins two larger areas of land, with water on both sides.
senses.example: The Isthmus of Panama connects the land of Central and South America.

senses.definition: A feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch.
senses.example: An itch on my arm woke me up.

senses.definition: To feel as if your skin needs scratching.
senses.example: My mosquito bite itched for two days.

senses.definition: One object or one entry in a group or list.
senses.example: The first item on our shopping list was bread.

senses.definition: A hard, pale material from the tusks or teeth of some animals.
senses.example: The museum label said that the old carving was made of ivory.

senses.definition: A soft white color like old ivory.
senses.example: We painted the wooden frame ivory.
